132 Practical Chemistry æERlMENT NO. 7 Object TO DETERMINE THE EQUIVALENT WEIGHT OF THE

A known weight of the metal is treated with excess of acid which has already been standardized. The volume of excess of acid (acid unused by metal) is calculated by titrating the acid against the standard alkali. by subtracting this volume from the volume of the acid taken, the volume of the acid consumed by the metal can be calculated. The equivalent weight of the metal can be calculated by knowing the volume of the acid used by the metal.

At the equivalence point: 1 gm equivalent of acid neutralizes 1 gm equivalent of metal. i.e., 1000 ml of N-acid = 1 gm equivalent of metal Hence, the equivalent weight of the metal will be the weight of the metal that has exactly combined with 1000 ml of N-acid.

Standardization of bench H2S04 (See the experintent no. 5)
Determination of the equivalent mass of the metal Clean the given metal (say, magnesium ribbon) with the help of sand paper. Weigh out about 0.23 gm of the metal accurately.
Introduce the weighed metal into a 250 ml volumetric flask.
Add a known volume of the standardized bench H2S04 (say 20 ml) into the volumetric flask with the help of a pipette.
After the reaction is complete (no more bubbles are seen), dilute the acid with distilled water. Make the volume up to 250 ml and shake well.

Titrate this acid solution against standard Na2C03 solution supplied (or, prepared by yourself) in presence of methyl orange indicator. At the end point, permanent faint pink colour is observed when the acid is taken in the burette.
Repeat the titration till you get at least two concurrent readings.
